newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat steady despite Egyptian purchase.
newsitem.headline: French wheat steady despite Egyptian purchase.

text.p: French wheat prices were steady on Monday, ignoring news Egypt bought 150,000 tonnes of French wheat over the weekend, dealers said.
Wheat into Rouen was quoted at 860 francs for spot delivery, 850 francs for November delivery and 835 francs for delivery from January onwards, unchanged from Friday.
On Saturday Egypt bought a total of 300,000 tonnes of wheat including 150,000 tonnes of French wheat at $146.50-$147 per tonne, Fob. Traders described these prices as "very low".
But dealers said the tonnages sold to Egypt were not large enough to boost French wheat prices as France, faced with a record wheat crop this year, needed to boost exports.
The low pricing of the French new wheat sale is also likely to spark to another tussle between exporters and the European Commission over wheat export subsidies, they said.
Exporters would need a refund of some 23 Ecus per tonne to help cover the sale, traders calculate.
Last week the EU nearly doubled the subsidy on wheat exports to 13 Ecus per tonne, to keep in line with falling world prices.
The award valued French wheat at some $160 per tonne, Fob.
